planting.note: Set divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained soil in partial shade; Majestic is a vigorous, strong-growing selection and benefits from being given a bit more room than smaller liriope cultivars.

directions: Majestic is a robust Liriope muscari cultivar prized for its large, showy spikes of deep lilac flowers held above dark green, half-inch-wide strap leaves. It tolerates heat, humidity, and periodic drought once established, performing reliably as a shaded border or mass groundcover planting. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Set divisions in spring in well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Ingwersen tolerates a wide range of conditions from drought to periodic wet soil once established.

directions: Ingwersen (sometimes sold as 'Classic Blue') forms dense clumps of glossy, dark green strap leaves topped from late summer into fall by tall, densely packed spikes of lavender-purple flowers, followed by persistent black berries. It is tough and adaptable, tolerating drought, wet soil, and a range of light from partial shade to fuller sun. Use as a long-blooming border edging or mass groundcover under high shade trees.

common_name: Marc Anthony Variegated Liriope (Tri-Color Gold-Edged Lilyturf)

planting.note: Set divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained soil in partial shade; this patented, award-marketed cultivar is grown chiefly for its unusually bright, multi-toned variegated foliage.

directions: Marc Anthony is a patented Liriope muscari selection whose new leaves emerge golden-yellow and green before maturing to a white-and-green striped variegation, giving the clump a shifting, multi-toned color display through the season rather than a single fixed variegation pattern. Pink-tinged lavender flower spikes appear in summer above the compact, 16-inch clumps. It is deer resistant and well suited to borders, edging, and container plantings in partial shade.

common_name: Silver Midget Dwarf Lilyturf (Compact Variegated Liriope)

planting.note: Set divisions in spring in well-drained soil in partial shade; its small, tidy scale suits tight edging and foreground plantings where full-size liriope would overwhelm the space.

directions: Silver Midget is a compact Liriope muscari cultivar with irregularly variegated dark green and cream leaf blades, distinguishing it from the solid-green dwarf cultivar 'Green Midget.' Lavender flower spikes appear in late summer above the low, tidy clumps, followed by black berries. Its diminutive scale makes it ideal for close-set edging, containers, and small-scale mass plantings in shaded borders.

planting.note: Set divisions in spring in well-drained soil in partial shade; this large cultivar needs more room than standard border liriope and is slow to require dividing.

directions: Densifolia is a large-scale Liriope muscari cultivar closely related to 'Evergreen Giant' in size and stiff-textured foliage, but distinguished by lavender rather than white flower spikes rising above the 18-24 inch clumps in summer. It tolerates heat, humidity, and periodic drought once established. Use where a bold, upright groundcover texture is wanted in a shaded border or beneath large trees.

common_name: Pusillus Dwarf Mondo Grass (Miniature Mondo Grass)

planting.note: Plant small divisions or plugs in spring or fall in part to full shade in moist, well-drained soil; being even more diminutive than standard dwarf mondo grass, set plugs on tight centers for faster fill.

directions: Pusillus is a miniature selection of mondo grass, forming dense tufts of fine, dark green foliage only an inch or two tall, smaller even than the popular 'Nanus' dwarf form. It is used chiefly as a moss-like accent between stepping stones, in Japanese-style plantings, and in small-scale shaded groundcover where a coarser grass would look out of scale. Small lilac-tinged flowers in summer are followed by blue-black berries, though the fine-textured foliage is the main draw.

common_name: Alba White Creeping Lilyturf (White-Flowered Spreading Liriope)

planting.note: Set divisions in spring in well-drained to average soil in partial to full shade; like the green-leaved species it spreads by underground stolons and is best confined with edging in smaller beds.

directions: Alba is a white-flowered form of the stoloniferous, spreading Liriope spicata, producing dense, erect spikes of white blooms in late summer above arching, finely-toothed dark green foliage on purple-brown stems. Like the species, it spreads aggressively to form a continuous weed-suppressing mat and excels under large trees or on slopes where fast colonization is desired. Shear old foliage to the ground in late winter before new growth emerges.
